legend: The bone marrow core biopsy is hypercellular (nearly 100%) and shows marked myeloid hyperplasia, with an increased myeloid-to-erythroid ratio and increased megakaryocytes with variable morphology, including some large hyperlobulated forms (<<36628>>). There are foci of marked eosinophilia (<<36629>>).

The bone marrow core biopsy is hypercellular (nearly 100%) and shows marked myeloid hyperplasia, with an increased myeloid-to-erythroid ratio and increased megakaryocytes with variable morphology, including some large hyperlobulated forms (<<36628>>). There are foci of marked eosinophilia (<<36629>>).
The bone marrow aspirate shows increased eosinophils and monocytosis (Giemsa).

Routine G-banded karyotyping (<<36631>>) shows a diploid male karyotype (46,XY[20]); however, due to a high index of suspicion, an eosinophilia FISH panel was performed (<<36632>>), which confirmed the presence of PDGFRB rearrangement using a dual-colour break-apart rearrangement probe hybridizing to 5q32 (spectrum orange on the centromeric side and spectrum green on the telomeric side of PDGFRB). Of note, 5q32 rearrangements are visible on routine karyotype in most cases of myeloid/lymphoid neoplasms with PDGFRB rearrangement, so this case represents a notable exception.

FISH with a break-apart probe for the detection of ETV6 rearrangements, with the telomeric 5′ probe labelled in green and the centromeric 3′ probe labelled in red, performed on bone marrow cells of a patient with t(5;12)(q32;p13.2): one interphase nucleus with a normal signal constellation (two red/green colocalization signals) and one interphase nucleus and one metaphase showing a split signal pattern for one ETV6 locus, indicating a translocation involving ETV6, are depicted; a red/green colocalization signal is present on the normal chromosome 12, whereas the derivative chromosome 5 carries a green signal and the derivative chromosome 12 carries a red signal (<<36717>>). G-banded karyogram of a patient with a t(5;12)(q32;p13.2) translocation leading to an ETV6::PDGFRB fusion, as confirmed by FISH with probes for PDGFRB and ETV6 and by RT-PCR (<<36719>>).
